claims.text: As-cast equimolar CoCrFeNiTi is a simple solid-solution alloy with relatively low hardness and strength.
As-cast equimolar CoCrFeNiTi has favorable plasticity and machinability.
The as-cast CoCrFeNiTi solid solution lacks controlled chemical short-range order.
The absence of chemical short-range order causes the relatively low hardness and strength of as-cast CoCrFeNiTi.
The absence of chemical short-range order leaves relatively few obstacles to dislocation motion in CoCrFeNiTi.
Dislocation-mediated processes can govern deformation and strengthening in compositionally complex alloys.
Annealing below the precipitation onset can induce a modest degree of chemical short-range order in equimolar CoCrFeNiTi.
Suitable annealing can alter chemical short-range order without forming secondary phases.
Annealing-induced chemical short-range order produces nanoscale chemically ordered clusters in CoCrFeNiTi.
Nanoscale chemically ordered regions impede dislocation glide.
Impeding dislocation glide through chemical short-range order will increase the yield strength and hardness of CoCrFeNiTi.
Chemical short-range-order strengthening can occur without drastically compromising the ductility of CoCrFeNiTi.
Annealed samples containing induced chemical short-range order will have higher hardness than the unannealed baseline.
Annealed samples containing induced chemical short-range order will have higher yield strength than the unannealed baseline.
Annealed samples will exhibit detectable local ordering and increased dislocation interactions relative to the baseline.
The proposed mechanism is limited to equimolar CoCrFeNiTi tested from 25 °C through 600 °C under compression or indentation without secondary-phase formation.
Failure to obtain statistically significant increases in both hardness and yield strength together with detectable induced ordering would falsify the proposed explanation.
